findings.title: pass_open's new sweep refusal makes every audit-changes round unopenable, and the same commit adds the protocol rule that guarantees it
findings.after:
if !sweep_ok
        missed = unswept(cfg, dir, isempty(prev_open) && scope === nothing ? [f["id"] for f in all_findings] : prev_open, fixrange)
        if !isempty(missed)
            println(io, "pass open: refused — the fix pass over $fixrange left a named location of an open finding untouched:")
            ...
            return 2
        end
    end
findings.why_it_matters: At pass 1 the ids handed to `unswept` are every banked finding, and `unswept` fires whenever a finding names a real file the range did not touch. The same change set writes into instruments/audit-changes/PROTOCOL.md step 4: "**This step never edits the tree.** `fixed` names a correction the NEXT change set carries" — so an audit round's dispose step touches nothing by design, and `unswept` will list every audit finding that quotes a real path. `close()` still refuses an audit round with `no graded pass` when `rec["passes"] == 0`, so `pass open` is on the audit's only path to closure. The result is that `gbg round pass open <audit-round>` now always exits 2 for audit-changes unless the operator knows to pass `--sweep-ok` — and instruments/audit-changes/PROTOCOL.md is the one protocol of the three that was NOT updated to say so (check-docs step 5 and check-consistency step 6 both were). The tool is its own fifth consumer, so this round is itself the first to hit it.
findings.description: The guard is written for the doc instruments, where a fix pass moves files between bank and pass open, but it is applied unconditionally in `pass_open`, which every instrument shares. For audit-changes the premise is false by the design this very commit records, and the refusal is total rather than incidental. Either the guard should skip `inst == "audit-changes"` (as it already skips seeded findings and the `scans` lane for exactly this kind of reason — "never fixed in the corpus"), or the audit protocol must name `--sweep-ok` as its normal invocation. As shipped, a correct audit workflow is refused by default and the operator learns it only from the refusal text.
findings.evidence: PROTOCOL.md (head): "**This step never edits the tree.** `fixed` names a correction the NEXT change set carries, which the next audit then covers; it does not mean \"corrected just now\"." — against Passes.jl:174 `missed = unswept(cfg, dir, isempty(prev_open) && scope === nothing ? [f["id"] for f in all_findings] : prev_open, fixrange)` and Passes.jl:122-124 which skips only `get(f, "seeded", false) || f["lane"] == "scans"`.

findings.title: unswept compares a whole-tree `named` set against a covered-paths-only `touched` set, so a fix outside src/test/ext/docs can never clear the refusal
findings.before: (no such check existed; pass_open went straight from the stamps to `findings = findings_of(dir)`)
findings.after:
function unswept(cfg, dir, ids, range)
    root = cfg["root"]
    touched = Set(Git.changed_paths(root, range, Preflight.covered_paths(cfg)))
    ...
        named = finding_files(root, f)
        isempty(named) && continue
        missed = [x for x in named if !(x in touched)]
findings.why_it_matters: `finding_files` keeps any path-shaped token in `locations` that `isfile(joinpath(root, f))` — the WHOLE tree. `touched` is `Git.changed_paths` restricted to `covered_paths(cfg)` = `["src", "test", "ext", "docs", "Project.toml"]` plus the `[paths]` entries, and a `[paths]` entry must be a directory (Config.jl:203). Every root-level file that is not a directory is therefore permanently un-sweepable: CHANGELOG.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md, IMPLEMENTATION.md, fleet.toml, .gitignore, .github/workflows/*. A check-docs finding quoting `CHANGELOG.md:12` or `fleet.toml:8`, fixed correctly in exactly that file, still appears in `missed` on every attempt, and the operator's only exit is `--sweep-ok`, which suppresses the check for every other finding in the same pass as well.
findings.description: The two sets are drawn from different universes. Either `finding_files` should keep only paths under the covered paths (so the guard judges what it can observe), or `touched` should be taken over the whole tree (`Git.changed_paths(root, range, ["."])`). As written, a legitimate, complete fix is reported as a half-fix, and the escape hatch is all-or-nothing rather than per-finding.
findings.evidence: Passes.jl:60-63 `for m in eachmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_./\-]*\.[A-Za-z0-9]+", String(l)) ... isfile(joinpath(root, f)) && !(f in out) && push!(out, f)` (no covered-path filter) against Passes.jl:121 `touched = Set(Git.changed_paths(root, range, Preflight.covered_paths(cfg)))` and Preflight.jl:400 `covered_paths(cfg) = unique(vcat(["src", "test", "ext", "docs", "Project.toml"], String.(values(cfg["paths"]))))`.

findings.title: The adjudicated and deferred closure channels close a finding without touching its files, and the new refusal blocks the pass that would record them
findings.before: (no check; every banked finding went to the verifiers and was closed by whichever of the four channels applied)
findings.after: (get(f, "seeded", false) || f["lane"] == "scans") && continue   # never fixed in the corpus; closed by rescan
findings.why_it_matters: Two of the design's own closure channels leave the finding's files untouched on purpose. `adjudicated` closes an id through a `scope = "finding"` entry in `.gbg/exemptions.toml` — outside `covered_paths` entirely, so it can never appear in `touched`. A deferral (`RULE.INST.FROZEN_MIDROUND`, carried by `carry_deferrals` from `<round>/deferred.md`) exists precisely because the fix is an instrument change that must be its own commit and release, so the quoted file is deliberately not edited in-round. `unswept` skips only `seeded` findings and the `scans` lane; both of these pass straight through it. A round in which the owner adjudicates one finding, or defers one, is refused at `pass open` and can only proceed by disabling the check for the whole pass.
findings.description: The skip list encodes exactly the right idea — "a finding that is not fixed in the corpus is not evidence of a half-fix" — but names only two of the four cases. Adjudication and deferral belong in it, or the refusal has to be per-finding rather than a whole-pass exit 2. The docstring's own escape ("for the fix that rightly lives somewhere else") concedes the case exists; it just makes the operator pay for it across every other finding.
findings.evidence: Passes.jl:123 `(get(f, "seeded", false) || f["lane"] == "scans") && continue` — the only two exclusions; against Passes.jl:487-489 "A fix pass that cannot make a change inside the round — an instrument change, which is its own commit and release — writes one line per deferral in `<round>/deferred.md`", and Preflight.jl:400, which puts `.gbg/exemptions.toml` outside every covered path.

findings.title: The only test covering pass_open in a normal round lifecycle was re-baselined from 0 to 2 in the same commit as the guard
findings.why_it_matters: The end-to-end lifecycle test is the package's only oracle for "a round opens a pass". It asserted exit 0 at base; at head it asserts exit 2 and then re-runs with the override. Nothing now pins the case the guard was written for — a pass that opens cleanly because the fix pass did sweep every named location — through the real `pass_open` entry point; the new unit test at test/rounds.jl:44-77 exercises `unswept` and `pass_scope` directly, never the refusal path inside `pass_open`. The change set thus removes the evidence that the ordinary path still works while adding the guard that closes it.
findings.description: Re-baselining the oracle in the same commit as the behaviour is the certifies-itself shape. The honest form here would be to make the lifecycle fixture sweep its findings' locations (a one-line touch of the quoted files before `pass open`) so the test still asserts 0, and to add a separate assertion for the refusal. As it stands, if the guard were later made unconditional or its escape removed, this test would keep passing.
findings.evidence: test/rounds.jl at base: `@test G.Passes.pass_open(cfg, round; io) == 0`; at head the same line reads `@test G.Passes.pass_open(cfg, round; io = devnull) == 2`, with the comment "this lifecycle plants verdicts instead of fixing, so it says so rather than pretending otherwise".

findings.title: check_paths' new docs_build scan adds a refusal the config schema makes unreachable and a per-token existence check that fires on any `.jl`-ending substring
findings.before: isfile(joinpath(root, "docs", "make.jl")) || push!(errs, "package.docs_build: docs/make.jl does not exist")
findings.after:
scripts = [String(m.match) for m in eachmatch(r"[^\s\"']+\.jl", cfg["package"]["docs_build"])]
    isempty(scripts) && push!(errs, "package.docs_build: names no .jl script to run")
    for s in scripts
        isfile(joinpath(root, s)) || push!(errs, "package.docs_build: $(repr(s)) does not exist")
    end
findings.why_it_matters: The stated defect — "a consumer whose command names another file was having a file it never runs checked" — cannot occur: `schema/config.schema.json` constrains `docs_build` with `"pattern": "docs/make\\.jl"`, unchanged by this diff, so every config that reaches `check_paths` through `Config.read`/`Config.parse` already contains `docs/make.jl`. The `names no .jl script to run` branch is therefore dead. What the change does add is live: the regex matches ANY substring ending in `.jl`, so a `docs_build` whose command line mentions a directory or flag ending in `.jl` — `julia --project=/home/g/Pkg.jl/docs docs/make.jl` yields the token `--project=/home/g/Pkg.jl` — is now a CFG.SURFACES FAIL, and CFG.SURFACES is in QUICK, so it fails `TestHarness.gate()` and the `makedocs` wrapper, not merely `gbg doctor`. This fleet's own paths carry spaces and `.jl` segments (CLAUDE.md: "Paths carry spaces (every consumer path has two): quote them in every rendered command"), and the regex excludes `"` and `'`, so a quoted path is chopped at the space and the tail is looked up as a relative file that does not exist.
findings.description: Wider than any defect it can fix, and the contract prose was rewritten to match: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's CFG.SURFACES row moved from "`docs_build` names `docs/make.jl` and that file exists" to "every `.jl` script the `docs_build` command names exists". The new oracle in test/config.jl reaches the asserted behaviour only by hand-merging a Dict — `Dict("docs_build" => "julia --project=docs docs/build_the_site.jl")` — that the config schema's own pattern refuses, so the test certifies a state no real consumer config can be in.
findings.evidence: schema/config.schema.json (head, unchanged by this diff): `"docs_build": { "type": "string", "pattern": "docs/make\\.jl" }`; ARCHITECTURE.md before: "# CFG.SURFACES requires it to name docs/make.jl", after: "# CFG.SURFACES requires the .jl it names to exist"; test/config.jl:15-16 `Dict("docs_build" => "julia --project=docs docs/build_the_site.jl")`.

findings.title: SCAN.SIBLING_LINK's new later-mention half is hard-tier and its link pattern matches any URL under the sibling's site, including a deep link
findings.before:
ok = m !== nothing && m.offset <= first(o) <= m.offset + ncodeunits(m.match)
            ok || push!(hits, Hit(file, n, "first mention of `$name` is not a link to $site: " * strip(raw)))
            break
findings.after:
if !seen
                seen = true
                linked || push!(hits, Hit(file, n, "first mention of `$name` is not a link to $site: " * strip(raw)))
            elseif linked
                push!(hits, Hit(file, n, "later mention of `$name` is a link, not a bare code span: " * strip(raw)))
            end
findings.why_it_matters: The scan is tier `hard`, so a hit fails `gbg scan docs`, the `makedocs` wrapper and any round's prepare — prose that built yesterday stops building today. `link_re = Regex("\\[`?" * name * "`?\\]\\(\\Q" * site * "\\E")` is a PREFIX match on the site, so a later, deliberately deep link — `[`GBGPeriodicFields`](https://grigorysarnitsky.github.io/GBGPeriodicFields.jl/api/grid/)` pointing a reader at one specific page — is reported as "a link, not a bare code span". The rule it cites is about mentions of the package, not about linking into its documentation, and a deep link after the first mention is a legitimate thing to write in a long guide page.
findings.description: The half being added was already written policy at base ("Later mentions in the same unit are bare code spans"), so enforcing it is licensed by RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK; the concern is that the check is wider than the rule and lands at hard tier with no triage step. Two files in this change set had to be edited to comply (fixture/GBG Fixture/docs/src/index.md and the fixture's prose_shape.csv re-baselined from 61 to 81 words), which is the corpus telling you existing prose was newly rejected. A narrower `link_re` — anchored to the site's own index, `\Qsite\E["')]` — would enforce the rule without foreclosing the deep link.
findings.evidence: src/Scans/sibling_link.jl:25 `link_re = Regex("\\[`?" * name * "`?\\]\\(\\Q" * site * "\\E")` — no terminator after the site; catalog/scans.toml SCAN.SIBLING_LINK `tier = "hard"` (unchanged); fixture/GBG Fixture/docs/src/index.md gained "It is read alongside [`GBGIsotropicTurbulence`](…), and a later mention of `GBGIsotropicTurbulence` is a bare code span, as the rule asks."

findings.title: SCAN.ARGS_FORM now counts a bare splat as an argument, so `f(cfg; kwargs...)` documented in prose becomes a hit
locations: src/DocLints.jl — the makedocs docstring rewritten in the same commit
findings.before:
const ARGS_BULLET = "The arguments are:"
const ARGS_PROSE = r"The arguments? (is|are) `"
...
        pos, kw = Reflection.signature_parameters(sig[nextind(sig, o):prevind(sig, c)])
findings.after:
const ARGS_BULLET = r"The\s+arguments\s+are:"
...
        splats(s) = [x for x in bare.(split(s, ',')) if occursin(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\.\.\.$", x)]
        append!(pos, splats(semi === nothing ? inside : inside[1:prevind(inside, semi)]))
        semi === nothing || append!(kw, splats(inside[nextind(inside, semi):end]))
findings.why_it_matters: `wants_bullets` is true for ANY keyword, so counting the bare splat flips every two-argument wrapper of the shape `f(x; kwargs...)` from prose-form-clean to "takes N positional and 1 keyword argument(s): the bulleted form, not prose". `kwargs...` is a pass-through, not an argument a reader is owed a bullet for — RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM's own exemption list already recognises that a wrapper documents no arguments at all. The change set then rewrote `DocLints.makedocs`'s docstring into the bulleted form, which is the corpus complying with a newly-widened scan rather than the scan finding a real defect. Symmetrically, making `ARGS_BULLET` whitespace-tolerant means a one- or two-argument docstring whose prose happens to wrap the phrase "The arguments are:" now trips the opposite branch, "bind them in running prose, not bullets".
findings.description: The tier is `triage` in both base and head, so this warns rather than fails a build — that is why it is minor and not major. Still, it is a widening of what the scan rejects that was not required by any defect the diff names: the comment justifies counting the splat only as "a parameter the rule counts", which the rule text does not say. The new `eltype_kw` exemption in the same hunk moves the other way and is well-founded, quoting the rule's own last clause.
findings.evidence: src/Scans/args_form.jl:42-44 "A splat is a parameter the rule counts, but `kwargs...` is not an identifier and `signature_parameters` drops it: without this, `f(cfg; kwargs...)` reads as prose-form." — against policy/docs-rubric.md RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM at base, whose exemptions are "a thin allocating wrapper, which documents no arguments at all; an internal `_`-prefixed helper …; and a single element-type keyword bound in one prose clause", none of which mentions splats.

findings.title: signature_fidelity's population no longer counts extension-homed bindings, adding a DEAD (exit 2) path for a package whose exports all live in an extension
locations: test/scans.jl:41-48 — the oracle added with it
findings.before:
examined === nothing || (examined[] += 1)                 # what was COMPARED: the scan's population
        if def === :extension
            push!(out, "$name: EXTENSION-HOMED (no methods loaded) — skipped"); continue
        end
findings.after:
if def === :extension
            push!(out, "$name: EXTENSION-HOMED (no methods loaded) — skipped"); continue
        end
        examined === nothing || (examined[] += 1)                 # what was COMPARED: the scan's population
findings.why_it_matters: `population == 0 && exempted == 0` is the DEAD verdict, and DEAD is exit 2 in `Scan.report` and a refused `prepare`. A package all of whose exported bindings are extension-homed with no methods loaded previously reported a non-zero population and passed; it now reports zero and is refused as "measured nothing", which is a cannot-evaluate verdict rather than a defect. That is arguably the honest reading — nothing WAS compared — but it is a new refusal for a tree that built before, and the only oracle added for it (test/scans.jl) asserts `n[] > 0` on the fixture, which has no such package shape, so the newly reachable exit-2 path is untested in the direction that matters.
findings.description: The move is correct on its own terms and the comment explains it well. Reported here only because it converts a previously-passing configuration into an exit 2 with no ledger route named in the message and no test in the failing direction; a consumer meeting it will read "measured nothing" and have nothing to do about it.
findings.evidence: src/Scan.jl:441 `dead(r) = r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0` with `code = 2`; test/scans.jl "signature_fidelity counts what it compared" asserts only `@test n[] > 0` and `@test n[] >= count(r -> !occursin("EXTENSION-HOMED", r), rows)`.
